nodes.label: A woman in her 70s had a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption lasting 1 month
Patient is a woman in her 70s with a 1-month history of pruritic and painful periorbital eruption

Medical history included lupus nephritis requiring hemodialysis, immune thrombocytopenia, acute myeloid leukemia, chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, deep vein thrombosis, diverticulitis, and postcolectomy diarrhea
Past treatments included hydroxychloroquine, which resulted in retinal toxic effects, and lenalidomide, which severely worsened platelet count with a nadir of 28 ×10^3/μL
Physical examination demonstrated scaly, crusted pink plaques involving the periorbital skin
Skin biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy
Direct immunofluorescence was not performed, so a lupus band could not be confirmed
Tissue microbiology and PCR testing were not performed, so infection could not be formally excluded
ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, and complement C3/C4 serologies were not performed or reported
Precise medication timeline was not available/reported, limiting assessment of drug eruption
Expert pathologist and laboratory physician favor lupus-related autoimmune process as the final diagnosis pending confirmatory tests
Skin biopsy was obtained from the affected left periorbital eyelid lesion
